504, 506 R/w Sec.34 of Indian Penal Code.

2. BRIEF FACTS OF THE PROSECUTION CASE ARE AS UNDER :
It is the case of the complainant that, on 16.02.2018 at about 5.45 PM, at No.42 belonging to CW.1 situated near Telephone Exchange, Veerabhadraswami Temple Road, Kothanuru, when CW.1 along with CW.4 taking the tailoring machine, by that Smt. It is further alleged that, CW.1 replied to the accused persons that the house belonged to her and the case is pending before the court, by that time accused No.1 outraged the modesty of CW.1 by holding her hand and pulled her here and there and assaulted her with hands on her cheek, when CW.4 proceeded to shoot the said incident in mobile, by that time accused No.1 broken the Samsung Mobile,

Based on the written complaint lodged by C.W.1, C.W.7 has registered the case against accused No.1 to 4 in P.S. Crime No.29/2018 for the offence punishable under section 341,
427, 323, 354, 506 R/w sec.34 of IPC.

Investigating Officers/CW.7 and 8 investigated the matter and after completion of investigation, CW.8 has submitted final report against the accused No.1 to 4 only for the offence punishable under section.341, 427,
323, 354, 504, 506 R/w Sec.34 of IPC.

3. Upon receipt of charge sheet, cognizance was taken for the offence punishable U/s 341, 427, 323,
354, 504, 506 R/w Sec.34 of IPC against the accused No.1 to 4 and registered the criminal case against them.
After registering the C.C.No.56530/2018 case, the accused No.1 to 4 have appeared and were released on bail.
Copies of the final report and its' enclosures were furnished to them in compliance of section 207 of Cr.P.C.
Sufficient grounds were made out to frame charge.

Hence,
charges framed and read over to the accused No.1 to 4.
They pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.

4. In order to prove the guilt of the accused No.1 to 4, the prosecution has examined seven witnesses out of 08 witnesses cited in the charge sheet as P.W.1 to 8 and relied upon Eleven documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11 and one mobile identified and got marked as MO.1 and closed its side.

Thereafter,
the accused No.1 to 4 were examined as provided U/s 313 of Cr.P.C by explaining incriminating evidence appearing against them.
The accused No.1 to 4 have filed their statement setting out details with regard to their defence.
The accused No.1 to 4 have denied the same.
During the cross examination of PW.1, 5 and 6, six documents have been confronted and marked through them as Ex.D.1 to Ex.D.6.
Accused persons have not led any of either oral or documentary evidence.
5. Heard both sides.
Perused the materials on record.

The points that arise for my consideration are;
1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, on 16.02.2018 at about 5.45 PM, at No.42 belonging to CW.1 situated near Telephone Exchange, Veerabhadraswami Temple Road, Kothanuru, when CW.1 along with CW.4 taking the tailoring machine to the first floor, by that time accused No.1 to 4 in furtherance of common intention have wrongfully restrained CW.1 and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.341 R/w Sec.34 of IPC ?

3. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, on the above said date,
C.C.No.56530/2018 time and place, accused No.1 to 4 in furtherance of common intention, among them accused No.2 and 4 have threatened CW.1 with dire consequences and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.506 R/w Sec.34 of IPC ?

4. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, on the above said date, time and place, accused No.1 to 4 in furtherance of common intention, among them accused No.1 assaulted CW.1 with hands on her cheek and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.323 R/w Sec.34 of IPC ?

5. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, on the above said date, time and place, accused No.1 to 4 in furtherance of common intention, among them accused No.1 outraged the modesty of CW.1 by holding her hand and pulled her here and there and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.354 R/w Sec.34 of IPC ?
C.C.No.56530/2018 6.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, on the above said date, time and place, accused No.1 to 4 in furtherance of common intention, when CW.4 proceeded to shoot the said incident in the mobile, by that time accused No.1 broken the Samsung Mobile phone,
caused loss and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.427 R/w Sec.34 of IPC ?
7. What order or sentence ?
7. My findings on the above points are as under :
Point Nos.1 to 6 : In the Negative.
 Point No.7 : As per the final order  for the following ;

As these six points are interlinked, I have taken up these points together for common discussion to avoid repetition of facts & evidence.
In order to bring home the guilt of the accused persons the prosecution has to establish that, the accused No.1 to 4 C.C.No.56530/2018 with a common intention have wrongfully restrained CW.1 and 4 and abused them in filthy language, assaulted Smt. 9. OCULAR EVIDENCE :-
In order to prove the above said allegations, the prosecution has examined the complainant/CW.1 as PW.1, wherein, she deposed that, on 16.02.2018 at 5.45 PM,
when she was shifting her tailoring machine towards first floor of her house, the accused persons wrongfully restrained her, accused No.2 hold her hand, accused No.1 hold the hand of CW.1 and misbehaved with her.

CW.1 has further deposed that,
accused persons have abused her in filthy language, threatened her with dire consequences and accused No.1 damaged the phone of the Son of the complainant,
who was making video-graphy.
10.

The prosecution has examined the panch mahazar witness CW.3 as PW.2,
wherein, he partly supported the case of the prosecution and identified his signature in the mahazar C.C.No.56530/2018 and also the mobile seized in the case as per MO.1.

The learned Sr.APP appearing for the state has treated the said witness as partly hostile and fully cross examined, wherein, he has admitted that, between 11.00 AM to 11.30 AM, mahazar was conducted, MO.1 was seized and CW.1 has shown the place of incident.

11. The prosecution has examined the son of the complainant i.e., CW.4 as PW.3,
wherein, he has supported the case of the prosecution and deposed that, on 16.02.2018, accused No.1 wrongfully restrained CW.1 and thrown tailoring machine from CW.1 and by holding her hand told not to come to the house.
PW.3 has further deposed that, accused No.4 has holded the hand of CW.1 and dragged her, accused No.3 abused CW.1 in filthy language and accused No.2 tried to assault CW.4 by stone.
PW.3 has further deposed that, the accused persons have threatened CW.1 with dire consequences.
PW.3 has further deposed that, when he tried to make the video-graphy of the incident, accused No.2 snatched the mobile.

12. The father of the complainant was examined as PW.4, wherein, he deposed that,
on 16.02.2018, CW.1 was C.C.No.56530/2018 shifting her tailoring machine to the first floor, at that time, the accused No.4 holded the hand of CW.1 and dragged her and wrongfully restrained CW.1.
PW.4 has further deposed that, when CW.4 tried to make videography of the incident, they thrown the mobile.
PW.4 has further deposed that, the accused persons have abused CW.1 in filthy language.

The learned Sr.APP appearing for the State has treated the said witness as partly hostile and fully cross examined him, wherein, he admitted the entire contents of the statement recorded before the police, which was suggested during cross examination of PW.4 by the learned Sr.APP.

The husband of the complainant was examined as PW.5, wherein, he deposed that, when the complainant intended to shift the tailoring machine, accused No.1 wrongfully restrained CW.1, abused her in filthy language.
Accused No.4 outraged the modesty of CW.1, accused No.2 damaged the mobile of the son of the complainant and made loss.

The learned Sr.APP appearing for the state has treated the said witness as partly hostile and with permission fully cross examined him, wherein, he admitted regarding entire contents C.C.No.56530/2018 of the statement, which was suggested during cross examination by Learned Sr.APP.
14.

The prosecution has examined the investigating officer i.e., CW.7 as PW.6, wherein, he deposed regarding the investigation being carried out by him from the inception of receipt of complaint,
registration of case, forwarding of FIR, drawing spot mahazar, seizure of Mobile i.e., MO.1.
15.

The prosecution has examined another investigating officer i.e., CW.8 as PW.7, wherein, he deposed regarding the investigation being carried out by him from receipt of records, appointed officials to apprehend the accused persons, receipt of documents, completion of investigation and filing of final report.

16 . ANALYSIS :-
Having gone through the ocular evidence, led in by the prosecution, before adverting to discuss on as to whether the prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubt, the allegations that putforth by the complainant against the accused persons are to be considered.

The complainant has C.C.No.56530/2018 alleged that, the accused No.1 to 4 in furtherance of common intention have wrongfully restrained her when she was shifting her tailoring machine to the first floor of her house.

The complainant has alleged against accused No.1 that, he has outraged her modesty by holding her hand, dragged here and there, misbehaved with her and took phone of CW.4, when he was making videography of the incident and broken down and caused loss.
The complainant has alleged against accused No.2 that he threatened CW.1 with dire consequences.
The complainant has alleged against accused No.3 that, she has abused her in filthy language.

The complainant has alleged against accused No.4 that,
he threatened her with dire consequences.
17. Having gone through the specific allegations made against the accused persons by the complainant, now it is necessary to consider the ocular evidence of the complainant and other witnesses.

CW.1/PW.1 in her examination-in-chief has deposed that, accused No.1 to 4 have wrongfully restrained, accused No.2 holded her hand, accused No.2 also holded her hand, outraged her modesty and misbehaved.
Accused No.1 took phone of CW.4 and damaged it.
Accused C.C.No.56530/2018 No.1 to 4 abused her in filthy language, threatened with dire consequences.

On perusal of the cross examination of PW.1, in conjoint reading of complaint and further statement of the complainant, it reveals that, the complainant has not averred about the accused No.1 misbehaved with her.

PW.1 has admitted that, there are CCTV Footages and also admitted with Smt. V.Vijayalaxmi vs Abhilash on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118636983/
6 regard to the mobile recording of the incident.

18. On perusal of the cross examination of PW.2, who is the seizure and spot mahazar witness,
wherein, he has admitted that, no notice has been given to him and contents of the panchanama were not read to him and got his signature.
PW.2 has pleaded ignorance as to with whom the mobile was and also he has not seen with regard to the document of the mobile.
At this juncture, relying on the ocular evidence of the investigating officer, CW.4, Panch Mahazar witness and on going through MO.1, no proper procedure for seizing the mobile has been carried out.
No documents have been produced in order to show that, the seized mobile belongs to CW.4.

In the absence of sufficient evidence and proper C.C.No.56530/2018 procedure being not followed, it would not be safe to rely on the ocular and documentary evidence led in by the prosecution and to conclude that the mobile i.e., MO.1 was seized at spot, wherein it belongs to CW.4.
No sufficient documents have been produced in order to show that, how much loss has been caused to the CW.4 in view of damaged to the mobile.
No specific averment made either in complaint or further sworn statement or statement of witnesses.
In such circumstances, the seizure of the material object creates suspicious in the mind of the court.
19. On perusal of the contents of the examination-in- chief of PW.4, it contradicts the contents of statement of PW.4 recorded before IO.

PW.3 during his cross examination has denied that, he has not produced any documents in order to show that, mobile belongs to him, however, admits that the said mobile was not having SIM Card and Battery in it.

PW.3 has further admitted that, there is no chit containing the signature of himself and panch mahazar witness on MO.1.
20.

On referring the contents of examination-in-chief of PW.4, he has deposed that, it is accused No.4, who holded the hand of CW.1 and dragged her, all the accused persons C.C.No.56530/2018 came to hit her, CW.4 tried to make videography of the incident and accused No.4 thrown the mobile and damaged it.
21.
On perusal of cross examination of PW.5 reveals that, he was not present as on the date of incident, he admits that he went to the spot after the incident.
On the other hand, it contradicts his own statement as he deposes that for two times he came to house No.42/1 in shifting the house hold articles.

At this juncture, I would like to refer Ex.D.2, which is the statement of CW.5 recorded before the police, wherein, he deposed that, CW.1 informed him about the incident to him through phone and thereafter, he went to the spot.

22. On referring the cross examination of PW.6, it reveals that, the accused persons had filed complaint against the complainant and others before filing the complaint in the present case, which is fortified by Ex.D.4.
IO has admitted that, he has not obtained the receipt of purchase of bill from CW.4.
IO has also admitted that, he has not made any independent witnesses in the case and he has not written in the mahazar that, there were no independent persons at the time of incident.
IO has also admitted that, he has not made C.C.No.56530/2018 investigation as to whether accused persons were on lease in the second floor of the house.

On perusal of cross examination of PW.7, he admits that he has not obtained CCTV footages.
PW.7 has admitted that, he has not obtained medical documents of CW.1 and 4.
PW.7 has also admitted that, the statement of CW.5 has been obtained after two months of the incident.
24. Ex.D.1 is the office copy of the Legal notice issued under the instructions of accused persons by their counsel to K.Ramesh Kumar, K.Govindaraj and Vijayalakshmi.

On referring the contents, it reveals that, the complainant and other persons have been called upon not to act on the sale deed dated:11.09.2015 and canceled the Sale Deed dated:11.09.2015 and 19.12.2015 and the Sale Deed executed dated:26.09.2016 was not binding upon the accused persons.
25. Ex.D.3 is the Sale Deed executed by one K.Ramesh in favour of the accused persons with regard to property No.4 of Kothanuru Village.

The schedule described in the Sale Deed is extracted here under for better C.C.No.56530/2018 understanding and for further discussions on the defence raised by the accused persons;

Ex.D.5 is the Certified copy of the PCR.No.54588/2018 on the file of XI ACMM, Bengaluru,
wherein, the accused No.2 has maintained private complaint against the complainant and two others alleging the commission of offence U/s 120A, 403, 415, 416, 418, 420, 423, 464, 468 of IPC.
The said matter was referred and FIR was registered against the above said persons for the above said alleged offences.

On perusal of Ex.D.5, the private complaint has been received at jurisdictional police on 17.04.2022.
28.
Ex.D.6 is the Certified copy of the FIR in crime No.52/2022, which has been registered on the basis of the private complaint lodged by the accused No.2 and same was referred to Kothanuru PS.

8 29.

The accused No.1 to 4 have filed their statement contending that, they are the owners of house property bearing Khata No.89/95/6 measuring East to West 51 feet, North to South - 29 + 39 / 2 feet intotal 1734 Sq.Feet, consisting of houses in Ground floor, First and Second Floor and have let the second floor to one Mahadevaiah.

Accused No.1 to 4 have C.C.No.56530/2018 contended that, in the year 2015 they have sold ground floor, first floor, one portion to K.Rameshkumar vide Registered Sale Deed, which is evident on going through Ex.D.3.
Accused No.1 to 4 have relied on Ex.D.1, Ex.P.4 and contended that, police complaint was filed on 07.02.2018.
Accused No.1 to 4 also contend that private complaint in PCR.No.54588/2018 was filed against complainant and her husband.
There are civil cases pending between the complainant and the accused persons to the property in question.
Therefore, prayed for acquitting them.
30. On perusal of the materials on record, in the year 2015 the accused persons have sold only Ground floor, first floor one portion to Ramesh Kumar, which is evident on going through Ex.D.3.
On referring Ex.P.3, the said Ramesh Kumar has sold the same through Sale Deed dated:19.05.2016 in favour of Vijayalakshmi.
In the said Sale Deed Second Floor house is not shown.
On perusal of Ex.D.1, the accused persons got issued legal notice dated:01.07.2017 pertaining to Sale Deed dated:19.05.2006.

On referring Ex.P.4, which is rectification Deed dated:14.07.2017 was got executed after issuance of legal notice by the accused No.2, which is marked C.C.No.56530/2018 at Ex.D.1, thereby the complainant in-corporated second floor house illegally.

On referring Ex.D.4,
police complaint was filed by the accused persons against the complainant on 07.02.2018.
Now I would like to rely on the date of incident, wherein, the complainant has alleged that on 16.02.2018 at 5.45 PM, incident took place.
In other words it reveals that to counter blast the complaint filed by the accused persons, the present complaint came to be filed.

31. On referring Ex.D.5, a private complaint in PCR.NO.54588/2018 was filed by the accused No.2 with regard to the rectification deed dated:14.07.2017 got executed by the complainant by in-corporating second floor house illegally for the offence of cheating.

The private complaint was referred to the jurisdictional police, inturn the police have registered FIR against complainant, her husband and Ramesh Kumar for the offence of cheating in crime No.52/2022, which is evident on going through Ex.D.6.
On referring Ex.P.8, it could be gathered that there are civil cases pending between the complainant and accused persons with regard to the property in question.
It has also come in the evidence that, there has been civil suit in OS.No.26519/2019 with regard to C.C.No.56530/2018 the 2nd Floor of the property.
It has also come in the evidence that, there is civil suit in OS.No.78260/2017 against the complainant.

The accused persons have filed Lease Agreement executed in favour of C.S.Mahadevaiah by accused No.2, though it is not marked,
however, the accused No.2 has leased the 2nd floor of property No.4 in favour of the said Mahadevaiah.
With regard to the same, there are civil cases pending against accused persons and CW.1 and others.
32. On over all perusal of the materials on record, the complainant initially has not alleged any specific allegations against the accused persons.
However, it is in the further statement of the complainant, she has alleged that the accused persons have committed the crime as alleged.

On referring Ex.P.11, which is a requisition and in conjoint reading of cross examination of IO, the complainant has refused to depose her statement before the Magistrate as provided U/s 164 of Smt. V.Vijayalaxmi vs Abhilash on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118636983/
9 Cr.

P.C. It is well settled that, the statement recorded before Magistrate as provided U/s 164 of Cr.P.C., is having greater value and has conclusive evidence with regard to the offence committed against women.
In the case on hand, the complainant has refused to tender her statement before Magistrate.

The C.C.No.56530/2018 evidence Tendered by PW.3, 4, 5 are none other than the son,
mother and husband of the complainant.
In other words, they are the related and interested witnesses.
IO has not enlisted any of the independent witnesses in the final report.
Though PW.1 admits that, she has video recordings of the incident, however, the IO has failed to produce the said video clippings and CCTV footages with regard to the incident.
No independent witnesses have been examined by the prosecution.
The IO has not collected the receipt of the mobile showing that, CW.4 is the owner of the mobile and also the prosecution has failed to prove the seizure of the said mobile.
The IO has not produced sufficient evidence in order to show that how much loss has been caused to the mobile of CW.4.
More particularly, the prosecution has failed to show that CW.4 is the owner of the mobile.

On referring the evidence of PW.1, 3 to 5, they are not deposed as to which of the accused have committed the crime as in consonance with the averments made in the complaint and further statement of the complainant, Statement of witnesses in specific terms.

In such circumstances, the case of the complainant becomes doubtful and there are material discrepancies in the evidence of PW.1 to C.C.No.56530/2018 7 in conjoint reading with the documentary evidence coupled with the ocular evidence of PW.1 to 7.
33.

On perusal of the materials on record, the evidence of the record led in by the prosecution both by oral and documentary evidence are not sufficient to conclude that the accused persons in furtherance of common intention have wrongfully restrained CW.1, accused No.1 outraged the modesty of CW.1 by holding her hand, dragged here and there, misbehaved with CW.1, damaged the phone of CW.4, accused No.3 has abused CW.1 in filthy language, accused No.2 and 4 have threatened CW.1 with dire consequences.
Therefore, the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, the benefit of doubt has to be extended to the accused persons and they are entitle for acquittal.
Having discussed so, I answer the Point Nos.1 to 6 are answered in the "Negative".
34. Point No.7:-

In view of the findings on above points, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER Acting under section 248(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused No.1 to 4 are C.C.No.56530/2018 acquitted of the offence punishable under sections 341, 427, 323, 354, 504, 506 R/w Sec.34 of Indian Penal Code.

The Bail bonds and surety bonds of accused No.1 to 4 shall be in force for the period of 6 months and thereafter it shall be canceled without further orders.
MO.1/ Mobile Phone being worthless is ordered to be disposed off in accordance with law after appeal period is over.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Smt. V.Vijayalaxmi vs Abhilash on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118636983/
7 23.
P.C. It is well settled that, the statement recorded before Magistrate as provided U/s 164 of Cr.P.C., is having greater value and has conclusive evidence with regard to the offence committed against women.
In the case on hand, the complainant has refused to tender her statement before Magistrate.
IO has not enlisted any of the independent witnesses in the final report.
No independent witnesses have been examined by the prosecution.
The IO has not collected the receipt of the mobile showing that, CW.4 is the owner of the mobile and also the prosecution has failed to prove the seizure of the said mobile.
The IO has not produced sufficient evidence in order to show that how much loss has been caused to the mobile of CW.4.
More particularly, the prosecution has failed to show that CW.4 is the owner of the mobile.
On perusal of the materials on record, the evidence of the record led in by the prosecution both by oral and documentary evidence are not sufficient to conclude that the accused persons in furtherance of common intention have wrongfully restrained CW.1, accused No.1 outraged the modesty of CW.1 by holding her hand, dragged here and there, misbehaved with CW.1, damaged the phone of CW.4, accused No.3 has abused CW.1 in filthy language, accused No.2 and 4 have threatened CW.1 with dire consequences.
Therefore, the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, the benefit of doubt has to be extended to the accused persons and they are entitle for acquittal.
